title: StepExecutionResult Contract

scope.purpose: Define the generic Step-level aggregate result returned by a concrete Step Instance to its owning Stage.
scope.appliesTo: Every concrete Step[TInput,TOutput], specialized as StepExecutionResult[TOutput].

contract.name: StepExecutionResult
contract.returnedAs: The structured result of one Step invocation, consumed by Stage Composition.
contract.responsibility: Carry the Step-level output artifact and the applicable Step-specialized validation, error, and error-handling aggregates composed from internal SPU and supporting-unit activity.
nonResponsibilities: Represent the result of an individual SPU invocation; that is SPUExecutionResult.
Expose internal SPU topology or individual component implementation details to Stage.
Define Stage-level or Pipeline-level status and flow policy.
Represent observability events, logs, telemetry, or Observation Unit results.

typeParameters.name: TOutput
typeParameters.meaning: The Step-specific type of the output artifact exposed to Stage through processingArtifact.
typeParameters.specialization: Selected by the concrete Step, not by an individual SPU unless the Step explicitly adopts the same type.

elements.name: processingArtifact
elements.meaning: The output artifact produced by the complete Step responsibility and exposed to its owning Stage.
constraints: Its type is exactly the Step's TOutput specialization.
The Step defines how zero or more SPU artifacts and other internal results contribute to it.
It is distinct from any individual SPU's processingArtifact unless the Step explicitly forwards one as its output.

elements.name: validatorResult
elements.producer: Step Composition from applicable validator-unit results
elements.meaning: The Step-specialized validation result or aggregate of validation results relevant to the Step invocation.
constraints: Concrete structure and aggregation rules are defined by the Step specialization and validator contracts.

elements.name: errorResult
elements.producer: Step Composition according to the Step Error Model
elements.meaning: The Step-level aggregate representation of selected SPUError occurrences and any other Step error information explicitly included by the Step Error Model.
constraints: Optional; detailed structure and semantics are defined by Step_Error_Model_Contract.json and its concrete specialization.
Preserves original producerSPUIdentity, occurrenceIdentity, full definition reference, and occurrence content as required by the Step Error Model.
Represents error information, not the outcome of handling that information.

elements.name: errorHandlerResult
elements.producer: Step-specific Error Handling Composition within Step Composition
elements.meaning: The Step-level aggregate of accepted error-handling operation entries produced by applicable Error Handling Units.
constraints: Its detailed structure and aggregation are defined by ErrorHandlerResult_Contract.json and the concrete Step specialization.
Does not contain, mutate, remove, or subsume errorResult.

optionality.representation: None in memory; null when serialized where serialization is defined.
semantics: Absence is not a universal status such as NotApplicable, NotExecuted, Success, or Failed.
Absence alone does not imply success or failure.
Applicability and interpretation are defined by the concrete Step.
Optional field presence remains distinct from a TOutput domain value that may itself permit null.

preservation.invariant: Every result required by the Step's concrete result contract that was actually produced and accepted into Step custody must be retained in the assembled StepExecutionResult, including results produced before a later internal failure.
rules: A later internal processing or supporting-unit failure does not authorize discarding an earlier retained result.
The Step must not fabricate a result for an operation that did not produce one.
Any result whose custody remains unresolved at a thrown-exception boundary is handled under the concrete Step's recovery contract; it must not be silently treated as absent.
processingArtifact, validatorResult, errorResult, and errorHandlerResult represent distinct information categories.
errorResult and errorHandlerResult must remain separate.
The aggregate carries Step-level results; it does not redefine the domain semantics of contributing component results.
SPUExecutionResult is an internal per-SPU invocation result and is not interchangeable with StepExecutionResult.

observationBoundary.rule: Observation events, logs, telemetry, and Observation Unit-specific results are outside the common StepExecutionResult contract unless a concrete Step explicitly defines a separate application-specific output integration.

rules: Step Composition assembles StepExecutionResult from the Step output and the applicable internal results actually produced and retained.
The Step defines the mapping/aggregation from SPUExecutionResult values to the Step-level processingArtifact and optional aggregate fields.
The Step Error Model defines ErrorResult structure and aggregation semantics; Step Composition performs the physical assembly.
The Step-specific Error Handling Composition aggregates accepted operation entries into ErrorHandlerResult; Step Composition integrates that result.
The contract does not prescribe a constructor, builder, mutation model, or implementation language.
The contract does not prescribe the internal execution order or topology.

explicitNonGoals: No universal execution status or success boolean is introduced.
No fixed validation-before-processing or processing-before-validation sequence is introduced.
No exception type, exception propagation policy, or catch boundary is prescribed.
No universal schema is imposed on StepValidatorResult, ErrorResult, or ErrorHandlerResult.
No Stage-level aggregation or Pipeline-level failure policy is defined here.
openDesignDetails: Define the concrete Step TOutput and its derivation from the internal SPU outputs for each Step.
Define concrete StepValidatorResult aggregation when multiple validator units are used.
Define concrete ErrorResult and ErrorHandlerResult type-parameter specializations for each applicable Step.
Define serialization only if StepExecutionResult must cross a process or persistence boundary.
